title_hint: Long founder pitch for a field-service software company raising a big seed
user_notes:
- arr 1.2m (mrr x12) 142 cust
- churn smb 2%/mo, nrr 108
- cac 4.5k, payback 11m
- ask 3-3.5m @12 pre = 10x arr, rich
- runway 10m, close by feb
- vp sales -> intro german guy
- partners mon

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Hi Priya, hi Tom, can you see my screen? Or, wait, no, you're sharing. Sorry.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Hi! Yeah, we see you fine. Tom's just, uh, getting coffee, he'll be right here.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: No worries. How was the offsite, you said you were away last week?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Oh it was good, Lisbon, super rainy though, which, nobody told us about.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Ha, classic. Okay, while we wait, I read the deck twice, so you can skip the intro slides.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Great, that helps. Tom's here, I think. Tom?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Yep, sorry, hi, I'm here. Morning, or, afternoon for you?

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Afternoon. Paris. Okay so let's jump in. Priya, give me the one-minute version anyway, for my notes.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Sure. So Halden builds scheduling and dispatch software for HVAC and plumbing companies, like, fifty to five hundred technicians.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Right, and the wedge is the mobile app for the technicians, which is, which is what they actually use all day, the office software is an afterthought.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: And how many customers today?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Hundred and forty-two paying, as of the end of September. Around, um, one point two million ARR.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Is that ARR or like annualized monthly revenue? Because those are different animals.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Fair. It's MRR times twelve, so, yes, annualized, contracts are mostly monthly. Annual contracts are about thirty percent now.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Okay. And growth, what was it year over year?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Last year we were at four hundred k, so, three x.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Nice. Net revenue retention?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: About one hundred and eight percent. Gross churn is, um, like two percent monthly on the small accounts.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Two percent monthly is a lot. That's twenty-odd percent annually.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Yeah, it's concentrated in the tiny shops, under ten techs. Above that it's, it's under one percent.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: So why take the tiny ones at all?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Honestly because self-serve brings them in cheap, CAC is, like, two hundred euros there. But we're, we're moving upmarket.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: What's blended CAC then?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Blended, around, uh, forty-five hundred. Payback eleven months.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: That's decent. How's the sales team built up?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: It's me and, and two AEs, plus a, a part-time SDR. Tom does the technical demos.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Which I love, said no CTO ever.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Ha. Okay. Tom, let's talk about the stack for a bit. What's the architecture?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: So, it's a, a Postgres backend, Kubernetes on a managed cloud, and the mobile apps are React Native. The routing engine is our own, it's the secret sauce, it's in Rust.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Why Rust?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Because the optimization has to run in, like, under two seconds for two hundred jobs. Python didn't cut it.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Got it. Security? These guys have customer addresses, access codes, that stuff.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: We have SOC 2 type one done, type two is in progress. And we did a pen test in the, in the spring.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Can I see the pen test summary?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Yeah, I can send you the executive summary, I'll just redact a few things first. I'll send it to you by Friday.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Perfect. Priya, what's the plan for the money? Raising how much?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: We're thinking, um, three million, maybe three point five. On, on, a seed extension, or, well, people keep calling it a 'serious a', but it's more like a big seed.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Okay. And what's the valuation expectation?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: We're anchored around twelve million pre. But we're flexible, if the right partner shows up.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: That's, ah, ten times ARR, which is, uh, rich for the churn you described.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: I mean, we know. Comparables are, they're at fifteen. But yeah.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Mmm. What's the structure, priced round or a SAFE?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Priced. We have one earlier SAFE with a cap of, uh, four million that converts.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: And who's on the cap table today?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Founders around sixty-two percent, the SAFE holders about eight, an ESOP pool at ten, and a couple of angels.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Okay. Can you send me the full cap table, with the pro rata rights flagged?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Sure. I'll send the cap table and the data room link by Friday as well.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Good. Let me just, uh, take a step back. What worries you the most about the next twelve months?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Honestly? Hiring a VP Sales. We've been talking to a few people but nobody's, nobody's quite the right fit.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Would you hire from outside the trade or from inside?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Inside, ideally, someone who sold to the HVAC distributors. But we might, we might also look at a head of partnerships instead. Not decided.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Yeah. I know a person who ran sales at a field-service company in Germany, maybe a good fit. I'll intro you to him next week.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: That would be amazing, thank you.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Tom's also been, um, wanting to...

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Sorry, to go back to the SOC 2 thing, it's type two, we're expecting the audit window to close in, uh, December.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Okay, good. What about competition? Who do you lose to?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Mostly to spreadsheets, which is the real answer. Then, uh, two big incumbents, and a couple of well-funded US startups.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: And in Europe?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: In Europe, only one, a Dutch company, they're about twice our size but their app is, um, it's honestly bad.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Mm. How do you win against them?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Price, local language, and the mobile experience. We also integrate with the accounting tools in Germany and France which they don't.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Okay. TAM, how do you size it?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: There's about three hundred thousand HVAC and plumbing firms in Europe above ten techs, no, wait, above five techs, sorry. At, like, five k a year average, that's one point five billion.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: That's a big number, but I'd rather think about the SAM, the, the, the countries you actually serve.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Yeah, DACH, France and Benelux, that's maybe forty percent of it.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Okay. Let's talk about burn.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Burn is about, hmm, one hundred and forty k a month net. We have ten months of runway at the current cash, so we want to close by, by February.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: That's tight. If it takes longer, what's the fallback?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: We'd probably do a bridge. If you guys are interested, I mean. Or we cut the burn.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Hypothetically, yes, we do sometimes bridge, but let's not plan on that.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Understood.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: What does the team look like? Headcount?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Twenty-three, with nine engineers, mostly remote across Portugal and Poland.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: And attrition?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: One regretted loss last year. Pretty happy.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: OKRs, do you run them?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Yes, quarterly. This quarter's big one is get churn under one point five percent in the SMB base. And, um, ship the new billing module.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: How's that billing module going?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: It's, uh, ninety percent. We've delayed it once already because Tom's team had a production incident.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Yeah, that was my fault, it was a bad database migration, we added an index in the middle of the day. Lesson learned.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: It happens. Who else is looking at the round?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: We have, uh, a couple of conversations. One fund in Berlin is interested, they asked for data room access.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: What's the timing there?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: They want to see us in two weeks, but we'd rather have a lead who's, like, the right fit.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Okay, and what are you hoping we'd bring?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Honestly, the network, we want to expand into Germany faster and your intro just now is a good start. And, and help with the board stuff and hiring.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Understood. Let me tell you how our process works. First I'll talk to my partners on Monday.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Okay.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: If they're excited, we'd do a second meeting with the full partnership, probably within two weeks. And then diligence.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Sounds good. And how, how do you typically price? Do you take the whole round or do you syndicate?

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: We usually lead with fifty to sixty percent, and co-invest with others. We'd want pro rata, of course.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Yes, we expected that.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Okay. A few more questions on the product. Tom, what's your roadmap for the AI stuff? Everyone asks.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: So, we, uh, we have a thing that suggests the likely parts a technician needs based on the job description. It works pretty well, like eighty percent.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: And we might, you know, add a voice assistant someday. Technicians can't type with gloves on.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: That's a good insight. But I wouldn't, I wouldn't prioritize it over the billing.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Agreed, it's just a someday idea.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Now customer concentration. Top customer as a percent of revenue?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Under four percent. Top ten is about twenty-two.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Good. What about pricing, per technician per month?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Thirty-nine euros per technician on the standard plan, and we're testing forty-nine with the AI parts suggestion.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Okay. Have you thought about usage-based pricing for the dispatch engine?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: We discussed it. Not now. Maybe next year.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Fine. What's the timeline for the SOC 2 type two report?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: I said December, I think. Yes, December.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Right, sorry. Okay. I think I have most of what I need. Anything we haven't covered?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: One question, which is, would you want to meet the rest of our leadership team? We have a head of customer success, Nina, she's great.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Yes, that would be great, we can do that in the second meeting.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Perfect. Also I already sent the deck and the financial model to your colleague yesterday, in case you didn't see.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: I saw, yes, thanks.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: And the model has the monthly cohort tab, which I think answers your churn questions.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Good, thanks.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Any other docs you'd like us to prepare?

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Customer references, three of them, ideally one of the small shops and one of the bigger ones.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Sure, I'll line up three references, I'll have names for you by next Wednesday.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Wonderful. Then I'll get back to you by Tuesday after our Monday partner meeting with a yes or no on a second meeting.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Perfect, we'll wait to hear.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Great. On my side, I'll take this to the partners as a lead candidate.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Thanks so much, you've been great.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Thank you both. Have a good weekend. Bye.

action_items.task: Send the pen test executive summary (redacted) by Friday
Send the cap table and data room link by Friday
Intro Priya to a contact who ran sales at a German field-service company next week
Line up three customer references and send names by next Wednesday
Reply by Tuesday with yes or no on a second meeting after the Monday partner meeting

decisions.text: Meet the rest of the leadership team in the second meeting
Take the company to the Monday partner meeting as a lead candidate

non_action_traps: Possible bridge round if the raise slips (hypothetical)
Voice assistant for technicians someday (idea, agreed it is not a priority)
Deck and model already sent yesterday (already done)
